identity.title: CRISPR mutagenesis of the MYC locus reveals a druggable ultraconserved RNA element.

content.abstract: Noncoding sequences comprise most of the human genome; however, their functional significance remains largely elusive. Using CRISPR tiling mutagenesis with near-PAMless, high-fidelity SpRY-Cas9, we mapped the fitness landscape of an entire human gene, the 10-kb MYC locus, at base-pair resolution. This unbiased interrogation revealed that 67% of functionally essential base pairs are noncoding. Essential noncoding base pairs are under strong constraint in the human population but show limited evolutionary conservation across species. Within this landscape, we identified an ultraconserved noncoding RNA element in the 3' untranslated region (UTR) that promotes perinuclear localization of MYC mRNA and nuclear localization of MYC protein through interaction with hnRNP L. Steric-blocking antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) targeting this element selectively eliminate diverse MYC-dependent cancer cells and inhibit growth of patient-derived tumor organoids. Together, these findings establish noncoding sequences as major carriers of functional genetic information and identify a therapeutically actionable RNA element whose targeting disrupts MYC-driven cancer.
